title: Illustrative hand-off: verify backup restoration
summary: Example only: a fresh session should verify that a database backup restores saved prompts and their provenance into an isolated database.
prompt:
This is an illustrative, agent-authored hand-off, not an owner instruction or permission to execute. Replace this sample with real session evidence before saving it. Current user instructions and cited authoritative records govern.

## Context and reason
A durable prompt store needs recoverable backups. A backup file existing is not proof that restoration works. This example makes no claim that a backup has been tested.

## Intended outcome and scope
When authorized, validate recovery using a separate disposable database; do not overwrite an active store.

## Durable evidence
Read the target project's checked-in backup and restoration instructions and inspect its actual backup format. Record exact paths and relevant commits in the real hand-off; this example has not checked them.

## Known hazards and uncertainties
A persistent Docker volume is not a backup. Restoring into the active database can destroy newer work. Backups may contain sensitive prompt text and must not be committed.

## Verification
Create a disposable database, follow the documented restore procedure, and compare project IDs, hand-off text, original session IDs, lifecycle states and versions with the chosen backup snapshot. Confirm the original database is unchanged. Record the commands actually run and their observed results.

source_metadata.note: Illustrative REST body. Use a real client/session ID and actual evidence before saving. For MCP save_handoff, also supply project_id.
